message.content:
### Quick Check from the Command Prompt  

Open **Command Prompt** (`cmd`) and paste:

```batch
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"
```

* What happens  
  * If Visual Studio Code is currently running, you'll see an entry similar to:

    ```
    Image Name                     PID Session name        Session#   Mem Usage
    ========================= ======== ================ ========= ==========
    Code.exe                    12345 Console                 1     150,000 K
    ```

  * If no such process exists, the output will say something along the lines of “INFO: No tasks are running which match the specified criteria.”

---

### Alternative – PowerShell

If you prefer PowerShell, this one‑liner does essentially the same thing:

```powershell
(Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
```

* It returns the process object when VS Code is running, otherwise nothing (or just `$null`).  
* You can also test explicitly:

  ```powershell
  if (Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
      Write-Host "VS Code is running."
  } else {
      Write-Host "VS Code is NOT running."
  }
  ```

---

### Using Task Manager (GUI)

Of course, you can always double‑click **Task Manager**, then look under the **Processes** tab for **Visual Studio Code** or simply search for `code`. This gives you more details (CPU/memory usage, start time, etc.).

---

#### TL;DR

Run `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"` in a normal command window. Any result means VS Code is alive; empty results mean it’s not.
